name: Hashcat - Attack Modes and Mask Charsets
description: The -a attack mode decides how candidates are generated; masks (?l ?u ?d ?s ...) drive brute-force and hybrid attacks. Custom charsets (-1..-4) let you define your own placeholder for targeted policy-aware cracking.

examples.label: Custom charset for a policy-aware mask

notes:
?a expands to ?l?u?d?s. Define up to four custom sets with -1/-2/-3/-4 and reference them as ?1/?2/?3/?4.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

variations.label: Attack modes (-a)
variations.command:
-a 0  - Straight (dictionary)
-a 1  - Combination (two wordlists)
-a 3  - Brute-force / mask
-a 6  - Hybrid wordlist + mask
-a 7  - Hybrid mask + wordlist

variations.label: Custom charsets
variations.command:
-1 ?l?u        # define set 1 = letters
-2 ?d?s        # define set 2 = digits+symbols
# then reference in the mask:
hashcat -a 3 -m 0 <hash> -1 ?l?u -2 ?d?s '?1?1?1?1?2?2'
